info.name: Nasaq — Master Verification Collection (financial · surcharge · grading · timetable · library · attendance)
info.description:
# Nasaq — Master Verification Collection

One self-contained run that exercises the whole system: academic setup, the full financial
module, the expatriate tuition surcharge, grading criteria, exams, and promotion.

## How to run it

1. Import this file into Postman.
2. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable if your server is not on `http://localhost:3000`.
3. Press **Run** on the collection and let it go top to bottom.

That is all. **There is no environment file, no OTP to copy out of the server logs, and no ID to
paste anywhere.** Every value chains automatically through collection variables, and the school
is registered fresh on each run with a timestamped slug — so you can re-run it as often as you
like without cleaning anything up.

## What the numbers are

Grade 1 tuition **8,000**, expatriate surcharge **15%**, sibling discount **10%**, 3-installment
plan.

| | سارة (SA — local) | أحمد (EG — expatriate) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Base fee | 8,000 | 8,000 |
| Surcharge | — | 1,200 |
| **Gross** | **8,000** | **9,200** |
| Sibling discount 10% | 800 | 920 |
| **Net** | **7,200** | **8,280** |
| Installments | 2400 x3 | 2760 x3 |

Both students are enrolled into the same class with an identical request. The only difference is
the nationality code on their profile.

## Decisions this collection encodes

- The surcharge is a **school fee**, not a government tax, so the discount applies to the
  post-surcharge amount. أحمد's discount is 920, not 800.
- Nationality is a **closed ISO list**. The dropdown is fed by `GET /nationalities`, and the API
  rejects anything outside it.
- A student with **no** nationality code counts as local — when the data is ambiguous, nobody is
  charged.
- Grading is **per term**. A subject across three terms keeps three criteria records and the
  yearly grade is their average.
- Additional fees stay **exact-amount only, with no refund** — a deliberate simplification.

## Folders

| Folder | Covers |
|---|---|
| 00-03 | School registration, settings, academic structure |
| 04-05 | Fee configs, plans, discounts, students |
| **06** | **Enrollment + surcharge — the core of the feature** |
| 07-08 | Discounts, payments, partial payments, corrections |
| 09 | Recalculation triggers: nationality, school settings, fee change |
| 10 | Changing a student's installment plan |
| **11** | **Failed enrollment must be retryable** |
| 12 | Bus, trips, additional fees |
| 13-14 | Grading criteria, exams |
| **15** | **Promotion preview — partially-graded years** |
| 16 | Validation guard rails |
| **18** | **Lectures & the weekly timetable, incl. clash detection** |
| 19 | Digital library |
| 20 | Assignments, activities, quizzes, projects |
| 21 | Attendance |
| **22** | **The teacher's day — timetable, attendance, preparation** |
| 17 | Admin read views |

Folders 06, 11, 15, 18 and 22 are where the important assertions live.

Folder 17 (admin read views) runs last so that everything it lists has been created first.

## When something fails

Open the Postman console. Every meaningful assertion is paired with a message that explains what
the failure means in plain terms — what a school would actually experience — rather than just
printing an expected/actual pair.

## Notes for the frontend

Look for requests whose description begins with **FRONTEND:** — they call out API shapes that are
easy to get wrong:

- `subjectId + academicYearId` does **not** identify one grading-criteria record.
- `subjectOfferingId` is always a string; `subjectOffering` is the populated object.
- `payments[]` is an append-only timeline; a refund sits next to the original payment.
- There is no combined "total owed" across the four balances.
- Promotion appends a new enrollment; it never overwrites the previous year.

---

**Updated 2026-08-13** for the backend changes merged that day: exam creation is restricted to teachers (folders 14 and 20 now author exams as a teacher), teacher attendance is live (21.8), GET /library/:id works (19.7), and students are refused on attendance (22.16, 22.17 — these were the bug reports and should now pass).
